stories.title: Shipping in Strait of Hormuz depends on US talks — Iranian Security Council chief
stories.summary: Mohsen Rezaei added that "an end to all conflicts in the Middle East," particularly in Gaza and Lebanon, was the top-priority condition for the resumption of vessel traffic
article_sentences: Future vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz will depend on negotiations between Iran and the United States, Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei said.

"At present, Iran has temporarily opened a corridor through the center of the Strait of Hormuz, but future shipping will depend on progress in negotiations with the United States," Rezaei said in an interview with Lebanon’s Al Manar TV channel.
stories.headline: Shipping in Strait of Hormuz depends on US talks — Iranian Security Council chief

opening: Future vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz will depend on negotiations between Iran and the United States, Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei said.
body: "At present, Iran has temporarily opened a corridor through the center of the Strait of Hormuz, but future shipping will depend on progress in negotiations with the United States," Rezaei said in an interview with Lebanon’s Al Manar TV channel.
Mohsen Rezaei added that "an end to all conflicts in the Middle East," particularly in Gaza and Lebanon, was the top-priority condition for the resumption of vessel traffic.
